# Observation resampling

## Objective

The `obs_resample` card defines an explicit, inspectable and reproducible evaluation plan before model training and tuning. Its purpose is to reduce data leakage and obtain performance estimates relevant to the intended predictions. Resampling alone does not prevent overfitting or guarantee independence.

The card stores split metadata in `proxy_data`, alongside the learning pipeline. It does not transform observations or add a pipeline step. Downstream training and tuning consume the same plan so that model comparisons use the same observations.

This is **evaluation resampling**: assigning observations to training and validation subsets. It is distinct from `targ_balance`, which changes weights or resamples observations **within a training subset**.

This document incorporates the review of the original proposal. Requirements below describe intended behavior, including additions to the existing `proxy_data` contract; they are not claims of implemented functionality.

## Prediction goals and roles

The footer offers **None / New observations / New strata / New entities / Future observations**. Exactly one prediction goal is active. Roles determine availability, variables and the resampling method; there is no separate objective, algorithm, grouping or stratification selector.

| Goal | Derived method and eligibility |
|---|---|
| New observations | Shuffled K-fold; automatically stratified by the assigned Stratifier when present. |
| New strata | Grouped K-fold using the Stratifier; enabled only when a Stratifier is assigned. |
| New entities | Grouped K-fold using repeated Identifier; enabled only for longitudinal data. |
| Future observations | Forward temporal splitting using Sequence; enabled when numeric or datetime Sequence is assigned. For longitudinal data, require validation identifiers to occur in training. |
| None | Pass incoming metadata through without this card's contribution. |

A unique Identifier identifies observations. A repeated Identifier requires an assigned Sequence, and the Identifier–Sequence pair must form a unique, nonmissing primary key. Repetition therefore establishes longitudinal structure. Invalid roles block active plans; resolve them upstream rather than asking for another interpretation in card settings. Support one variable for each split role in this version.

A Stratifier has two distinct uses, resolved by the footer goal: preserve proportions for New observations, or withhold whole levels for New strata. Numeric values explicitly assigned this role are treated as discrete levels; do not infer bins or use a Target as an implicit Stratifier. New entities and Future observations address different longitudinal prediction tasks. Combined future-time/unseen-entity separation remains deferred.

**Development** rows are available for model selection. A generated split divides them into **training** and **validation** subsets. Explicit Partition validation rows instead define a supplied model-selection split. **Final holdout** rows are reserved for evaluation after selection; **prediction** rows are reserved for unlabelled predictions. **Unused** identifies observations outside a particular split's windows or gaps.

A target is not required for structural construction. Supervised execution requires one Target and complete labels outside prediction rows. Warn when New observations ignores dependence suggested by Identifier or Sequence. Geometry does not automatically determine spatial splits; retain a TODO for spatial blocks, buffers, coordinate systems and units.

## Partition mapping

Support one Partition variable with two or more observed, nonmissing levels. Settings contain a table with **Level / Rows / Purpose**, using one dropdown per observed level. Choices are **Unassigned / Development / Validation / Final holdout / Prediction**.

Every observed level must have exactly one explicit assignment, and at least one level must map to Development. Multiple levels may share a purpose. Never infer assignments from frequencies or automatically accept recognizable labels. Missing values and incomplete assignments block the plan. Save mappings by variable and typed level identity, not row position.

If any levels map to Validation, use those rows as one predefined validation subset, with Development as training. Keep all settings visible and enabled; K and temporal-window settings are irrelevant for supplied validation. Otherwise derive internal development splits from the footer goal. Final holdout and prediction subsets can coexist and never enter training or validation during tuning.

Check all boundaries against the selected goal. New strata/entities requires group separation. Future observations requires earlier training than validation, and earlier combined development/validation than each final reserved subset. For longitudinal future predictions, validation and reserved identifiers must already occur in the corresponding fitting data. Never redraw a supplied boundary to make it pass.

After model selection, final refitting may use Development plus explicit Validation rows. Final holdout and Prediction remain separate: consumers must select the intended reserved subset when both exist. Missing targets are allowed only in Prediction rows, which cannot be scored locally.

## Resampling strategies

### Predefined validation

Use the explicit Development and Validation assignments as one training subset and one validation subset. Final holdout and Prediction rows remain excluded. There is no randomization. These validation results may guide model selection, so they must not be presented as an untouched final-test estimate.

### Ordinary K-fold

Divide development observations into `K` folds. Each observation appears in validation exactly once and in training for the other `K - 1` splits. Default to five folds and reproducible shuffling with a stored integer seed of `42`. Require `2 <= K <= N`, where `N` is the development row count; a default that is infeasible must be corrected explicitly.

### Stratified K-fold

Use the same coverage rule while approximately preserving the proportions of the assigned Stratifier levels. Require at least `K` development observations in every observed stratum. Missing stratification values block the plan. Do not claim that stratification handles dependent observations.

### Grouped K-fold and leave-one-group-out

Assign each group wholly to one validation fold. No group may occur in both training and validation within a split. Grouped K-fold caps `K` at the number of distinct development groups; fold row counts may differ substantially. Randomly permute whole group levels using the stored seed and distribute them evenly across folds. Use `min(requested K, number of development groups)` and report any reduction in the footer Status. At least two development groups are required; row counts can differ between folds.

Leave-one-group-out creates one split per group and requires at least two groups. Show the resulting number of model fits before training. Every development observation is validated exactly once in either grouped strategy.

Stratified grouped K-fold is deferred: keeping groups intact and preserving category proportions are separate constraints. In particular, a group identifier cannot also have every one of its levels represented in every fold.

### Forward temporal splitting

Use the assigned sortable numeric or datetime Sequence variable with no missing values. Sort its distinct values ascending and keep all observations sharing a value together. Use a common ordering across entities; identifiers are not independent clocks. Entity-relative sequence values require upstream alignment before this strategy can represent a common forecast date.

The first version measures windows in **distinct Sequence values**, not rows or elapsed time. Show this unit beside every setting and show actual date/value ranges in the preview. Irregular spacing is allowed, but equal-sized windows may span different durations.

Let `T` be the number of distinct Sequence values in development data, indexed `0, ..., T - 1`. Define:

- `W`: initial training-window size, a positive integer.
- `H`: validation-window size, a positive integer.
- `G`: gap between training and validation, a nonnegative integer.
- `S`: step between splits, a positive integer; default `H` and require `S >= H` in the first version to avoid overlapping validation windows.
- Window mode: **Expanding** (default) or **Fixed**.

For split `j = 0, 1, ...`, let `b_j = W + jS`. Using half-open ranges of Sequence-value positions:

| Membership | Sequence-value positions |
|---|---|
| Expanding training | `[0, b_j)` |
| Fixed training | `[b_j - W, b_j)` |
| Gap, unused in this split | `[b_j, b_j + G)` |
| Validation | `[b_j + G, b_j + G + H)` |

Generate every complete split satisfying `b_j + G + H <= T`. The split count is derived, not independently editable:

`M = max(0, 1 + floor((T - W - G - H) / S))`.

Require at least one complete split. Remaining observations are unused in that split; do not shrink a final window to include a partial remainder. Earlier validation observations may enter later training windows as time advances. Never shuffle temporal splits.

For example, with `T = 12`, `W = 5`, `H = 2`, `G = 1`, and `S = 2`, expanding training ranges are `[0, 5)`, `[0, 7)`, and `[0, 9)`; validation ranges are `[6, 8)`, `[8, 10)`, and `[10, 12)`. In fixed mode the corresponding training ranges are `[0, 5)`, `[2, 7)`, and `[4, 9)`.

A gap controls separation of observation times only. It does not establish that labels or features were available at prediction time; overlapping outcome horizons and delayed labels need additional rules, deferred below.

## Data and pipeline contract

### Stable source and row identity

Construct memberships against `proxy_data.clean_frame`, the stable post-cleaning source, rather than `proxy_data.frame`, which may be a fitted full-data preview or contain resampled rows. Split-role variables must be available in that source. Preview-only derived columns cannot define membership in the first version.

All exported indices are **zero-based integer positions in that source frame**, never pandas index labels. Duplicate index labels are therefore allowed. Display ordering is separate from source ordering: temporal sorting must map back to the original positions without reordering the exported data.

### Proposed metadata

Add an evaluation-plan value to `proxy_data` with this logical content; exact Python type and field names are implementation choices:

| Content | Required information |
|---|---|
| Recipe | Schema and splitter version, strategy, prediction objective, selected variables, partition mapping, window/fold settings and seed where relevant. |
| Source identity | Source revision or fingerprint covering row membership/order and relevant split values and roles. Row count alone is insufficient. |
| Reserved membership | Separate explicit validation, final-holdout and prediction positions, if present. |
| Validation membership | Ordered split identifiers and their train/validation source-position arrays, materialized or generated deterministically. |
| Diagnostics | Validity, blocking reasons, warnings, coverage, and per-split counts and checks. |

These indices address the complete source frame even when development data excludes a reserved subset. A downstream consumer that passes a development-only frame to sklearn must explicitly remap indices into that frame's coordinate system.

Changing source membership, row order, split-variable values, roles or settings regenerates or invalidates the plan. Changes to target values refresh target diagnostics; changes to model inputs invalidate downstream fitted results even if memberships are unchanged. Training must check source compatibility before consuming a plan. Do not reuse stale arrays because the new dataset has the same length.

Bookmarks store the compact recipe and source-compatibility information, not every membership array. On restoration, regenerate and validate against the restored source. The card regenerates a fresh plan against the current source and splitter version; incomplete level assignments still leave it unready. Preserve metadata through compatible `proxy_data` copies; source-changing operations must explicitly invalidate it.

### Downstream execution

For each split, fit a fresh clone of the complete learning pipeline using only its training positions from `clean_frame`. Fit imputers, encoders, feature selectors, scalers and balancing operations within that subset; apply the fitted transformations to validation data. Never use the full-data preview as the input to evaluation. This follows sklearn's [guidance on avoiding preprocessing leakage](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html#data-leakage).

The splitter is supplied to evaluation or tuning as a splitter or iterable of `(train_indices, validation_indices)`; it is not a transformer inside the pipeline. sklearn calls the second array `test_indices`, even when it serves model-selection validation here. See the [`cross_validate` interface](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.cross_validate.html).

Training-only balancing runs after membership selection. Duplicated or synthetic training rows never become validation, final-holdout or prediction observations. This card does not change evaluation weighting policy.

After model selection, refit a fresh pipeline on Development plus explicit Validation rows and evaluate the Final holdout, or produce predictions for Prediction rows. When both reserved subsets exist, the consumer must select which it is requesting. Record that a holdout was used; subsequent choices informed by its results mean it no longer supplies an untouched final evaluation. Without a final holdout, label reported scores as validation/model-selection estimates.

## Front screen

Show a heat map with observations on the x-axis and splits on the y-axis. Use stable, distinct colors and a visible legend for **Training / Validation / Unused / Final holdout / Prediction**; show only applicable states.

Add a separate Stratifier strip beneath the splits whenever a Stratifier is assigned. For non-temporal goals, sort by Stratifier, preserving source order within levels. Without a Stratifier, use group order for grouped splits and source order otherwise. Future goals always keep Sequence primary, including predefined temporal validation. Label the ordering explicitly. The compact view shows the strip and short label; fullscreen adds category legends, sorted-stratum boundaries and hover counts. Aggregated bins show the most frequent membership or stratum in both strips; ties use membership legend order or the first stratum in source order. Hover details identify the source position, split, membership and relevant group or Sequence value. Reserved observations retain their reserved state in every split.

Above the chart, summarize the objective, strategy, development/reserved counts, number of splits and whether supervised checks are complete. Display blocking errors and warnings prominently. Never show a stale successful chart as the current valid plan.

Bound the rendered heat map for large datasets by aggregating contiguous display positions. Color each bin by its most frequent membership, breaking ties in legend order, with all counts available on fullscreen hover. State that the display is aggregated; never sample or aggregate the actual split memberships.

## Flip-side

Show one row per split with training, validation and unused counts; group counts and overlap where applicable; Sequence ranges; target-class counts where available; and diagnostic status. Show reserved counts and overall validation coverage separately.

Provide downloadable membership data in long form: `split_id`, `source_position`, `membership`, and optional original index label, group and Sequence value. Preserve zero-based source positions in the download. Generate the export on demand rather than retaining a wide table with unequal-length columns.

## Settings and footer

The footer contains the prediction goals above, defaulting to None. Keep all goals selectable and explain missing or invalid roles in the footer status and Settings. Preserve a selected goal on role changes, but mark its plan invalid rather than silently selecting another goal.

Settings contain the Partition mapping, **Number of folds (K)**, the random seed for generated observation and group splits, or temporal windows/gap/step/mode for generated Future observations splits. A Stratifier, Identifier or Sequence is taken from its assigned role; do not expose redundant variable selectors. K equal to the number of groups gives leave-one-group-out behavior without a separate algorithm button.

Changes to footer goals or relevant settings regenerate the plan automatically after `@this.settle(seconds=2)`. All settings remain visible and enabled; irrelevant settings neither affect the recipe nor trigger recalculation. Footer `Status` uses a themed span: secondary for pass-through, primary for progress or K adjustments, success for ready plans, warning for cautions, and danger for blocking errors. None passes incoming metadata through. A later active card replaces the incoming plan rather than combining independent plans. An invalid active selection blocks guarded downstream training; never reuse the previous valid plan or silently fall back to ordinary K-fold.

Bookmarks save goal, numerical settings, level-purpose mappings and source compatibility information. Regenerate exact memberships when compatible. Source changes and older recipe versions regenerate a fresh plan automatically; newly observed Partition levels still require purpose assignments. Do not reuse stale memberships.

## Validation and acceptance criteria

Block publication of a ready plan when any required structural check fails:

- Every index is unique within its subset, in bounds and tied to the current source; training and validation are nonempty and disjoint.
- Reserved rows never occur in development training or validation. Every source row has an explained state for each split.
- Required split variables exist and have no missing values. Fold, group, stratum and window counts satisfy the selected strategy's rules.
- Grouped splits have zero train/validation group overlap; temporal splits respect the stated ranges, gaps and strict ordering of training before validation.
- For a categorical Target, every training subset contains every class observed in development data. Report absent validation classes as warnings because some metrics may be undefined. Downstream scoring must also check its metric-specific requirements and report unavailable scores explicitly.
- Predefined reserved boundaries satisfy the declared group or temporal objective. Missing targets block supervised execution where labels are required, without silently dropping rows.

The implementation must demonstrate reproducible memberships for the same source, recipe and supported splitter version; exactly-once validation coverage for K-fold/grouped strategies; correct temporal ranges including tied Sequence values; correct behavior with duplicate pandas labels; and correct invalidation after filtering or reordering.

Integration checks must demonstrate that holdout/prediction rows never fit preprocessing or balancing, that validation rows never fit them during tuning, preview row duplication cannot alter membership, source-to-development remapping is correct, and bookmark restoration regenerates the same compatible plan. Invalid plans must not silently fall back to ordinary K-fold.

## Deferred extensions

- Automatically generated final holdouts that preserve the selected group or temporal constraints.
- Multiple Partition variables, predefined multi-fold assignments, and simultaneous competing plans.
- Stratified grouped K-fold, repeated random holdout, repeated CV, bootstrap evaluation and nested CV.
- Combined unseen-entity/future-time evaluation; elapsed-time windows; entity-relative clocks; overlapping validation horizons; and purging based on label availability or outcome intervals.
- Automatic spatial splitting. A future design must specify existing regions versus generated blocks, block size, coordinate reference system, distance units, exclusion buffers, missing geometries and undersized regions. Explicit region grouping is already possible, but does not guarantee spatial independence across boundaries.

The [sklearn cross-validation guide](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) provides reference implementations for standard splitters. Pythagoras-specific source identity, role interpretation, temporal-value windows and display behavior remain part of this card's contract.

## Summary

**Name:** `obs_resample`

**Mutable:** Yes, for evaluation metadata; observations and the accumulated learning pipeline remain unchanged.

**Output:** One goal-derived validation plan, optionally with separate predefined final-holdout and prediction subsets.

**Training integration:** Supplies memberships to downstream training and tuning, which fit independent pipelines within training subsets.

## Modelling context and initial survival support

The card records a versioned `ModellingContext` on `proxy_data`, independently
of evaluation membership. “Use incoming context / infer from Target” preserves
upstream declarations. Automatic outcome inference distinguishes numeric regression,
nominal/Boolean classification and ordered categorical classification; explicit
choices handle numeric class codes. No single Target leaves automatic task inference
unresolved. A changed context invalidates existing evaluation membership.

The initial survival implementation supports one baseline row per subject, one
terminal event, and right censoring. Settings declare exact duration/event column
names, observed-event and censored codes, duration units and origin. Duration is
finite, numeric and nonnegative; outcome values must be present outside Prediction
partitions. Censoring is an observed status, not a missing outcome. `model_predictors`
excludes declared outcome components as well as Target columns. Downstream model
consumers must use this accessor rather than treating all source columns as inputs.

Survival evaluation checks event counts and follow-up ranges in every training and
validation fold. Event stratification is available by assigning the event column a
Stratifier role and selecting it. Folds without events are reported as invalid.
Comparable-pair and censoring-support checks remain the responsibility of the future
metric evaluator; readiness here establishes structural validity, not metric validity.
Prediction rows may have unknown outcomes. Final holdout remains outside tuning.

Repeated subject records and temporal survival objectives produce an explanatory
invalid-plan status. Temporal support requires fold-specific administrative censoring
and calendar-based label-availability rules, which are not implemented in this stage.
Other censoring types, delayed entry, competing risks, recurrent events, time-varying
covariates and survival metric horizons are deferred. Spatial evaluation retains its
existing dependence warning. These limitations must not be advertised as supported
capabilities by the later model catalogue card.

Context configuration also applies when Predicting is Nothing: no new evaluation
plan is generated, and an incoming plan is invalidated if its outcome context changed.
Settings are persisted through the card's ordinary configuration mechanism.
